Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>, Legal <legal@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Q: retention exceptions + extractability for audit logs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP response so far. A couple of follow-ups from our security and legal teams around audit trails:

1) We need confirmation that audit logs can be exported on-demand as tenant-scoped snapshots (filters by tenant ID + time window) with a tamper-evident manifest. Our compliance folks want to run quarterly independent attestations.
2) We also need a retention-exception workflow: sometimes we need to preserve logs beyond the normal retention window for legal holds. Can you describe the mechanics and SLA for applying and later removing a legal hold?
3) Preferred delivery: S3-compatible object with server-side encryption + pre-signed URL, or direct encrypted transfer to our SFTP. What do you support?

I've attached a simple CSV with our expected export schema for reference (audit_log_schema_v2.csv).

Can you send a short plan (export cadence, max payload, approximate time-to-export for 30-day vs 3-year windows) by next Tue? Procurement is pushing the timeline.

Thanks — happy to set a brief call if useful.

Tim Hayes
Director, IT Compliance
Aurora Health Systems
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFP Q: retention exceptions + extractability for audit logs

Hi Tim —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers up front, details below and an attached draft retention matrix (retention_matrix.xlsx) that maps RJ (Redwood) capabilities to your requirements:

- On-demand tenant-scoped snapshots: supported. We can export tenant-scoped slices (tenant_id + time range) as compressed newline-delimited JSON objects. Each export includes a signed, tamper-evident manifest with SHA-256 checksums for each object.
- Legal hold / retention exceptions: we support per-tenant legal holds that stop automated deletion and tag data as "preserved". Holds can be applied via API or Console; removal requires a recorded approval and a retention-change audit entry (immutable).
- Delivery options: S3-compatible with SSE (AES-256) and pre-signed URLs, or SFTP push. We can also provision a temporary, encrypted one-time transfer endpoint for high-volume transfers.

Proposed next steps and timelines:
- Small window export (30 days, up to 10 GB): typical completion < 2 hours.
- Large window export (3 years, dependent on tokens/rows): estimate 6–48 hours; we parallelize by shard and provide progress updates.
- Delivery: initial export to S3 pre-signed URL by default; if SFTP is required, add 24 hours for endpoint configuration.

I'll coordinate internally to confirm the tamper-evidence details (manifest signing, custody chain). Can we do a 30-minute call Thu to agree on delivery and legal-hold workflow?

Best,

Marissa / Ben —

Short answers for Aurora and Legal:

1) Manifest & signing:
- Exports are produced as a set of compressed objects (gzipped ndjson). For each object we compute a SHA-256 checksum. We generate a manifest (JSON Lines) that lists object name, byte-size, checksum, and UTC timestamp.
- Signing options: enterprise customers may elect HSM-backed signing (we integrate with customer KMS/HSM where available) OR Redwood-managed signing keys. For HSM-backed signing we store the signing key metadata in the customer's control plane and perform signing operations in an isolated signing service; signature provenance is recorded in the manifest header.

2) Legal hold workflow:
- Legal hold is a first-class API resource. Applying a hold creates an immutable event in the audit ledger (who/when/reason). The hold prevents downstream retention jobs from deleting data.
- Removal: hold removals require an approver with role scoped permissions; removal also emits an immutable audit entry and a pre-removal export snapshot is offered automatically for chain-of-custody.

3) Delivery / SLA constraints:
- Small exports (< 10 GB): usually complete in under 2 hours.
- Medium (10–500 GB): 6–24 hours depending on shard counts and region.
- Large (> 500 GB): 24–72 hours; large deliveries will be staged into chunked objects and delivered via pre-signed S3 URLs.
- SFTP provisioning: typically 24–48 hours to set up whitelisted IPs and credentials.

Operational notes:
- We retain an immutable audit ledger for all hold operations and export requests; the ledger entries are stored for the customer's retention period plus an additional 90 days for forensic traceability.
- Export payloads are salted and hashed; we provide verification tools (CLI) to validate checksum and signature.

I attached a short runbook we can share with Aurora. If they want HSM signing we should scope a KMS integration quote.

Laura Bennett
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Delivery: S3 pre-signed URLs with SSE-AES-256 (default) or SFTP push. HSM-backed signing & KMS integration available for enterprise accounts (additional configuration/quote).
